{{DISPLAYTITLE:Timeline of events in ''Pokémon the Series''}} [[File:RegionsMoviesMap ReUpload.jpg|thumb|450px|A map of the [[Hoenn]], [[Johto]], [[Kanto]], and [[Sinnoh]] [[region]]s as of {{aniseries|DP}}; locations of {{pkmn|movie}}s are deliberately marked, and labeled {{OBP|Pokémon|species}} are positioned in relation to the locations of certain episodes.]] This is a chronological list of significant events in ''[[Pokémon the Series]]'' and the episodes which they occurred in, or, for events which happened outside the series, where they happened in relation to the episodes. ==Passage of time== It is worth noting that, while there are events that may mark the passage of time during the main storyline of the {{pkmn|animated series}}, most characters show little sign of aging. This is most striking for the young characters who are generally the main characters. Flashbacks often show characters when they are younger. In {{aniseries|PTS}}, {{Ash}} is identified as 10 years old from [[EP001|the first episode]][https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Zyt2GKb6qWw&t=120s Pokémon – I Choose You! [FULL EPISODE] | Pokémon: Indigo League Episode 1 - YouTube]: "And now that I'm ten, I can finally get my Pokémon license." to the end of the [[S25|25th season]].Ash's [https://www.pokemon.co.jp/tv_movie/anime/ character profile] (in Japanese) mentions that he is 10 years old as of ''[[Pokémon Journeys: The Series]]''. While this issue is largely unexplained, the [[Pokémon.com]] {{DL|Pokémon.com|mailbag}} did [http://web.archive.org/web/20030402094510/http://pokemon.com/letters/2002916.asp address] Ash's age in September 2002.
Ash Ketchum was indeed ten years old when he started, but he is ageless – since the beginning of the show until now, Ash has become an icon, a legend, like Mickey Mouse. But Mickey Mouse doesn’t look 75 years old (although he is), and the same goes for Ash.

([[SM005]]) |} ===''Pokémon the Series: The Beginning''=== {{main|Timeline of events in Pokémon the Series: The Beginning|Timeline of events in ''Pokémon the Series: The Beginning''}} {{aniseries|OS}} marks the start of Ash's quest to become a [[Pokémon Master]] as he sets off in the [[Kanto]] region. Beginning in [[Pallet Town]] with his [[first partner Pokémon]], {{AP|Pikachu}}, he faces numerous challenges and captures new Pokémon. Throughout his journey, he battles the [[Gym Leader#Indigo League|Gym Leaders]] to earn eight badges, starting with his first at the [[Pewter Gym]], while frequently thwarting Team Rocket's nefarious schemes. Ash's first adventure culminates at the [[Indigo Plateau Conference]], where he demonstrates his growth as a Trainer, after ultimately earning his final Badge and qualifying for the [[Indigo League|regional Pokémon League]]. Following the league, Ash briefly returns to Pallet Town, where {{an|Professor Oak}} assigns him the task of visiting the [[Orange Islands]] to retrieve the mysterious [[GS Ball]] on his behalf. While traveling through the archipelago, Ash adds {{AP|Snorlax}} and {{AP|Lapras}} to his party and meets [[Professor Ivy]]. After getting the GS Ball from her, Ash and Misty decide to continue exploring the islands, while Brock stays behind as Professor Ivy's assistant. They soon encounter [[Tracey Sketchit]], a [[Pokémon Watcher]], who joins the group as Ash sets his sights on taking on the [[Orange League]]. ===''Pokémon the Series: Gold and Silver''=== {{main|Timeline of events in Pokémon the Series: Gold and Silver|Timeline of events in ''Pokémon the Series: Gold and Silver''}} In {{aniseries|GS}}, Ash continues his quest to become a [[Pokémon Master]] as he travels through [[Johto]] with his Pikachu, along with Misty and Brock as his [[Ash's friends|traveling companions]] again. Starting from [[New Bark Town]], he decides to collect all eight [[Johto League|Johto Gym Badges]] and sets his eyes on the [[Silver Conference]]. He faces off against [[Gym]] Leaders [[Falkner]], [[Bugsy]], [[Whitney]], [[Morty]], [[Chuck]], [[Jasmine]], [[Pryce]], and [[Clair]]. On his journey, he makes {{an|Casey|new friends}}, catches {{AP|Heracross}}, {{AP|Chikorita}}, {{AP|Cyndaquil}}, {{AP|Totodile}}, {{AP|Noctowl}}, and receives a [[Pokémon Egg]] from a kind [[Mr. Shellby|elderly]] [[Kimie|couple]]. The trio encounters [[Legendary Pokémon]] such as {{OBP|Suicune|recurring}}, {{p|Entei}}, and a {{OBP|Silver|Lugia|duo}} of {{OBP|Lugia|Silver's parent|Lugia}}, and they participate in events like the [[Whirl Cup]]. Ash also reunites with [[Ritchie|old friends]] and rivals, including {{an|Gary}}. At the Silver Conference, he manages to defeat Gary and confronts {{jo|Harrison}} in the [[EP271|quarterfinals]]. After the tournament, Ash bids a touching [[EP273|farewell]] to Misty, the new [[Cerulean Gym]] Leader, and Brock, and returns to Pallet Town. After a [[EP274|short break]], he reaffirms his passion for learning about new Pokémon and makes up his mind to travel with Pikachu to a [[Hoenn|new place]]. ===''Pokémon the Series: Ruby and Sapphire''=== {{main|Timeline of events in Pokémon the Series: Ruby and Sapphire|Timeline of events in ''Pokémon the Series: Ruby and Sapphire''}} In {{aniseries|AG}}, Ash embarks on a new journey to the [[Hoenn]] region, accompanied by Pikachu and joined by new friends {{an|May}} and [[Max]], as well as the returning {{an|Brock}}. Beginning his Hoenn journey in [[Littleroot Town]], Ash sets out to compete in the [[Hoenn League]], while May initially plans to follow her [[Norman|father]]'s [[Gym Leader|footsteps]], but later decides to pursue the goal of becoming a top [[Pokémon Coordinator]]. Along the way, Ash adds [[Ash's Sceptile|Treecko]] to his [[party]], Brock finds a [[Brock's Marshtomp|Mudkip]] to join him, and May chooses [[May's Blaziken|Torchic]] as her first partner Pokémon. The group encounters [[Team Aqua]] and [[Team Magma]], Hoenn's villainous teams, as well as Legendary Pokémon such as {{OBP|Groudon|Ruby and Sapphire series}} and {{OBP|Kyogre|Ruby and Sapphire series}}. As Ash challenges the region's Gym Leaders to earn his eight Gym Badges, May begins competing in [[Pokémon Contest]]s, earning [[Ribbon]]s as she develops her skills as a Coordinator. She competes in the [[Hoenn Grand Festival]], advancing through the rounds but facing her skilled rival [[Drew]] in the quarterfinals. Meanwhile, Ash's efforts culminate at the [[Ever Grande Conference]], where he faces strong rivals like [[Tyson]] and [[Morrison]]. After the League, he learns about the {{OBP|Battle Frontier|Generation III}} and decides to take on this new challenge, while May continues to pursue her goals in Pokémon Contests across Kanto. The group returns to Pallet Town, reuniting with familiar faces like Misty and Professor Oak, before setting off on their next adventure through the Battle Frontier. Ash challenges the [[Frontier Brain]]s for their [[Symbol]]s. His new quest's first stop is the [[Battle Factory]], where he reunites with {{AP|Charizard}} and battles Factory Head [[Noland]] and his fearsome [[Noland's Articuno|Articuno]], earning his first Symbol. Alongside May, Max, and Brock, Ash travels across Kanto, facing other Frontier Brains like [[Greta]], [[Tucker]], and [[Lucy]], earning symbols through intense battles. During this time, May continues to hone her skills as a Pokémon Coordinator, earning Contest Ribbons throughout Kanto as she works toward competing in the [[Kanto Grand Festival]]. As Ash approaches the final stages of his Battle Frontier challenge, he faces Pyramid King {{an|Brandon}} but loses. After multiple attempts, he earns the Brave Symbol, securing his place in the Battle Frontier [[Hall of Fame]] and is offered the chance to become a Frontier Brain. Both May and Ash compete in the [[AG191|Terracotta Contest]], leading to a tie between them in the final round. Afterward, Ash and his friends part ways, with May heading to [[Pokémon Contest#Johto Contests|Johto]] to continue her journey as a top Coordinator. Back in his hometown, Gary challenges Ash with a [[Gary's Electivire|new Pokémon]] from the [[Sinnoh]] region. This discovery excites Ash, leading him to prepare for his next adventure in Sinnoh with Pikachu and his stowaway, {{AP|Aipom}}. ===''Pokémon the Series: Diamond and Pearl''=== {{main|Timeline of events in Pokémon the Series: Diamond and Pearl|Timeline of events in ''Pokémon the Series: Diamond and Pearl''}} In {{aniseries|DP}}, Ash arrives at the [[Sinnoh]] region, accompanied by his Pikachu and, initially unbeknownst to him, Aipom. He is soon joined by a novice Pokémon Trainer {{an|Dawn}} from [[Twinleaf Town]], and later, his long-time friend Brock. Aiming to follow in her mother [[Johanna]]'s footsteps as an aspiring [[Pokémon Coordinator]], Dawn begins her journey with {{TP|Dawn|Piplup}} after rescuing the Penguin Pokémon from an {{p|Ariados}}. Ash also meets [[Paul]], a Trainer from [[Veilstone City]] whose harsh training methods with his {{TP|Paul|Chimchar}} create tension between him and Ash throughout the series. As part of his [[Pokémon Triathlon|personal growth]], Ash adds new Pokémon to his team, such as {{AP|Starly}} and {{AP|Turtwig}}, while Dawn captures {{TP|Dawn|Buneary}} and {{TP|Dawn|Buizel}}, gradually working on her skills as a Trainer and a Coordinator. Throughout their travels, the group [[Pokémon Dress-Up Contest|encounters]] various [[Hearthome City Tag Battle Competition|challenges]], including battling [[Gym Leader]]s, participating in [[Pokémon Contest]]s, and [[DP131|facing off]] against formidable rivals. As their journey progresses, Ash, Dawn, and Brock confront the [[DP150|sinister plans]] of [[Team Galactic]], who seek to control the Legendary Pokémon {{p|Dialga}} and {{p|Palkia}}. With the help of their Pokémon and [[Looker|allies]] like [[Professor Rowan]] and [[Cynthia]], the trio works to counter Team Galactic's efforts, ultimately [[DP152|liberating]] the {{an|lake guardians}} {{p|Mesprit}}, {{p|Azelf}}, and {{p|Uxie}}. Meanwhile, Dawn competes in [[DP114|numerous]] Contests, steadily earning Contest Ribbons and overcoming [[Pokémon Ping Pong Tournament|personal challenges]]. She breaks her losing streak at the [[Wallace Cup]], after defeating May, Ash and Brock's former traveling companion. Dawn makes it to the [[Sinnoh Grand Festival]] with her fellow Coordinator friends and rivals, such as {{si|Kenny}}, [[Zoey]], [[Nando]], and [[Ursula]]. While Ash earns all eight [[Sinnoh League]] Gym Badges and participates in the [[Lily of the Valley Conference]], he faces formidable opponents like Paul, {{an|Barry}}, [[Conway]], and Nando. His rivalry with Paul culminates in a three-episode quarterfinal battle, where [[Ash's Infernape]] proves its strength and growth, leading Paul to realize his own shortcomings and respect Ash. They both promise to battle again in [[JN114|the future]]. In the climax of the Sinnoh League, Ash battles {{si|Tobias}}, a powerful Trainer who uses Legendary Pokémon like {{p|Darkrai}} and {{p|Latios}}, ultimately placing in the [[DP189|Top 4]]. Following the league, Dawn [[DP191|decides]] to remain in Sinnoh to focus on her growth as a Coordinator, while Brock is [[DP190|inspired]] to pursue a career as a [[Pokémon Doctor]]. Ash and Brock return to their home region of Kanto, with Ash reflecting on his growth and achievements in Sinnoh. The series concludes with Ash setting the stage for [[BW001|future]] challenges and adventures. [[Team Rocket]] also undergoes promotions and receives new directives, hinting at ongoing conflicts, while Ash’s experiences in Sinnoh reinforce his determination to become a Pokémon Master. ===''Pokémon the Series: Black & White''=== {{main|Timeline of events in Pokémon the Series: Black & White|Timeline of events in ''Pokémon the Series: Black & White''}} In {{aniseries|BW}}, Ash Ketchum takes a flight to the [[Unova]] region, accompanied by his ever-loyal Pikachu. He is joined by an aspiring [[Type expert|Dragon Master]] and adventurous young Trainer named {{an|Iris}} from the [[Village of Dragons]], as well as a passionate [[Pokémon Connoisseur]] and then-Gym Leader from [[Striaton City]], {{an|Cilan}}. Upon arriving in the new region, Ash learns that Unova primarily features entirely new Pokémon not found in any of the regions he previously visited. Aiming to challenge the [[Unova League]] by defeating a new set of Gym Leaders, he finds another rival in [[Trip]]. In the Unova region, Ash captures all three of the region's first partner Pokémon: {{AP|Oshawott}}, {{AP|Tepig}}, and {{AP|Snivy}}. Iris begins her journey with Ash using her {{TP|Iris|Axew}} and {{TP|Iris|Excadrill}}, while Cilan has a {{TP|Cilan|Pansage}}. Their team dynamic evolves as they navigate through various trials, leading to Ash earning his first Unova League Badge at the [[Striaton Gym]] by taking on Cilan and his two brothers, [[Cress]] and [[Chili]]. As the journey unfolds, Ash and his friends confront the more organized schemes of Team Rocket, who aim to harness the powers of the three [[Forces of Nature]] and {{an|Meloetta}}. Alongside capturing new Pokémon, Ash participates in the [[Pokémon World Tournament Junior Cup]], along with a familiar face, {{an|Dawn}}, and a new rival, {{un|Cameron}}. The series' first overarching arc culminates with the [[Vertress Conference]], where Ash faces formidable opponents and engages in a challenging battle against Cameron in the quarterfinals. Back in [[Nuvema Town]], upon the league's conclusion, the stage is set for further adventures when [[Professor Juniper]] informs Ash of a new Gym in [[Aspertia City]]. En route to the {{an|White Ruins}}, Ash and his friends meet the enigmatic {{an|N}}, who shares a unique bond with Pokémon, doesn't like [[Pokémon battle]]s as he views them as forced fights, and is later revealed to have a complex history with the villainous [[Team Plasma]]. Together with Ash and co., they confront Team Plasma's scientist [[Colress]], who is developing technology to manipulate Pokémon. Ash further strengthens his party, when {{AP|Charizard}} rejoins his team and assists in battles against Team Plasma. As Team Plasma's ambitions escalate, our heroes finally arrive at the [[White Ruins]], where [[Ghetsis]] plans to revive {{an|Reshiram}} using the [[Light Stone]]. With the help of Looker, [[Anthea and Concordia]], the gang thwart Team Plasma's plan, freeing the controlled Pokémon and leading to Ghetsis, Colress, [[Aldith]] and [[Barret]]'s arrests. With Team Plasma disbanded, N departs with Anthea and Concordia with his vision of harmony between humans and Pokémon. Meanwhile, Ash [[BW123|shares]] with Professor Juniper that he wants to return to his hometown, Iris confesses that she wants to learn more about {{type|Dragon}}s from other regions, and Cilan express a hope to continue his adventures to be a top class Pokémon Connoisseur. Ash, Iris, and Cilan journey through the Decolore Islands as they make their way back to [[Kanto]] from the Unova region. Along the way, they meet {{an|Alexa}}, a journalist from [[Lumiose City]] in the [[Kalos]] region who introduces them to her {{p|Helioptile}} and {{p|Gogoat}}, two Pokémon native to her homeland. Ash participates in the [[Scalchop King Competition]] with his {{AP|Oshawott}}, a tournament for Trainers who raise male {{p|Oshawott}} and {{p|Dewott}}. The group also encounters old acquaintances like [[Clair]], the [[Blackthorn City]] Gym Leader, providing {{an|Iris}} an opportunity to further her goal of becoming a Dragon Master by battling and learning from her. As they [[BW141|reach]] Kanto, Iris and Cilan decide to part ways to pursue their own ambitions—Iris heads to the [[Johto]] region to train with Clair, while Cilan goes to hone his skills as a [[Pokémon Connoisseur]]. Ash returns to [[Pallet Town]] with Alexa, reunites with his [[Delia Ketchum|mother]] and Pokémon. After learning about the Kalos League from Alexa, and the fact that [[Viola|her sister]] is one of the Gym Leaders, he makes up his mind to embark on a new journey, setting the stage for his next adventure in ''[[Pokémon the Series: XY]]''. ===''Pokémon the Series: XY''=== {{main|Timeline of events in Pokémon the Series: XY|Timeline of events in ''Pokémon the Series: XY''}} In {{aniseries|XY}}, Ash arrives in the [[Kalos]] region, where he meets {{an|Clemont}}, an inventor and former Gym Leader of [[Lumiose City]], and his younger sister [[Bonnie]]. Soon after, Ash reunites with his childhood friend [[Serena]], whom he first met at a summer camp in Pallet Town. She joins him on his journey and aims to become a [[Pokémon Performer]]. Together, they travel across Kalos and meet [[Professor Sycamore]], who specializes in [[Evolution]] and [[Mega Evolution]]. Ash catches new Pokémon like {{AP|Froakie}}, which eventually evolves into {{AP|Greninja}}, forming a [[Bond Phenomenon|unique bond]] known as "Ash-Greninja" that [[XY100|enhances]] their battling {{a|Battle Bond|abilities}}. During his journey, Ash challenges various Gym Leaders, including an intense [[Lumiose Gym|Gym]] battle against Clemont in Lumiose City, where he [[XY067|earns]] the Voltage Badge. Serena pursues her dream of becoming the [[Kalos Queen]] by participating in [[Pokémon Showcase]]s, competing against rivals like [[Shauna]], [[Nini]], and [[Miette]]. The group becomes involved with the mysterious phenomenon surrounding [[Squishy]], a Zygarde Core that Bonnie befriends. They also repeatedly cross paths with [[Alain]], a Trainer working for [[Lysandre]] of [[Team Flare]], who is researching Mega Evolution and collecting Mega Evolution energy. Ash and Alain develop a rivalry, with Ash striving to master his Greninja's unique transformation. During the [[Lumiose Conference]], Ash battles his way to the finals by defeating [[Sawyer]] in the penultimate match. Facing off against [[Alain]] in the final battle, he ultimately finishes as runner-up. Shortly after, Team Flare launches an attack on Lumiose City, aiming to control Zygarde and reshape the world according to Lysandre's vision. This prompts Ash and his friends, along with Alain, the Kalos Gym Leaders, and Champion [[Diantha]], to work together to stop Team Flare's plans. In the climactic battle, Bonnie's companion "[[Squishy]]" reveals itself as a [[Zygarde Core]], combining with [[Z2|another Core]] to transform into Zygarde's Complete Forme and successfully thwart Team Flare's ambitions. With peace restored in Kalos, Serena decides to become a [[Pokémon Coordinator]] and pursue [[Pokémon Contests]] in the [[Hoenn]] region, accepting a new path for her performances. Clemont returns to his Gym in Lumiose City with Bonnie, who aspires to become a Trainer like her brother some day. Ash [[XY140|bids farewell]] to his friends and heads back to [[Pallet Town]], concluding his adventures in the Kalos region. ===''Pokémon the Series: Sun & Moon''=== {{main|Timeline of events in Pokémon the Series: Sun & Moon|Timeline of events in ''Pokémon the Series: Sun & Moon''}} Venturing into the tropical paradise of the [[Alola]] region in {{aniseries|SM}}, Ash arrives with his mother Delia and [[Mimey]], eager to experience new adventures. Immersed in a world of exotic Pokémon and unique customs, he enrolls in the [[Pokémon School]], where he befriends classmates {{an|Lana}}, {{an|Lillie}}, {{an|Mallow}}, {{an|Sophocles}}, and {{an|Kiawe}}. Gifted a [[Z-Ring]] by the guardian deity {{DL|Guardian deities (anime)|Tapu Koko}}, Ash embarks on the [[island challenge]], aiming to master powerful [[Z-Move]]s and overcome the grand trials of each island. Alongside his new friends, he discovers the wonders of [[Poké Ride|Ride Pokémon]], encounters [[Alolan form|regional variants]], and catches Pokémon like {{AP|Rowlet}}, {{AP|Rockruff}}, and {{AP|Litten}}, who grow stronger as they tackle various challenges. The group faces rivals such as {{an|Gladion}} and contends with the mischief of [[Team Skull]], while [[Team Rocket trio]] make their presence known in Alola, encountering unique Pokémon and [[SM025|acquiring]] their own [[Z-Crystal]]. As their journey unfolds, Ash and his companions become entangled in the mysteries surrounding the [[Aether Foundation]] and the emergence of [[Ultra Beasts]] threatening the region. Befriending a {{p|Cosmog}} nicknamed [[Nebby]], which eventually evolves into the Legendary {{p|Solgaleo}}, the group forms the [[Ultra Guardians]] to protect Alola from inter-dimensional threats. Together, they confront the formidable {{an|Necrozma}}, striving to restore light to {{AP|Poipole}}’s darkened homeworld. Ash's bond with his Pokémon deepens as his Rockruff evolves into a rare Dusk Form {{p|Lycanroc}}, and Litten evolves into {{p|Torracat}} during an exhilarating [[Battle Royal]] with the {{an|Professor Kukui|Masked Royal}}. The climax arrives with the inaugural [[Alola League]] at the [[Manalo Conference]], where Ash battles through intense matches against skilled Trainers, including his rival Gladion. Emerging victorious, he becomes Alola's first-ever [[Pokémon Champion|Champion]]. However, the celebrations are interrupted by the appearance of multiple menacing {{DL|Ultra Beasts (anime)|Ultra Ruin Guzzlord|Guzzlord}}, prompting a united effort to protect the region once more to send them back to [[Ultra Space]]. Following this, Ash engages in an epic [[Full Battle]] in an exhibition match against Professor Kukui, with Tapu Koko joining as Kukui's final Pokémon, culminating in a spectacular Z-Move [[SM144|clash]]. With the conclusion of the Alola League, Ash's friends pursue their own dreams: Sophocles aims to visit the [[Mossdeep Space Center]] with [[Molayne]], Lana seeks the mythical {{p|Manaphy}} in the ocean depths with [[Lana's father|her father]], Mallow aspires to expand to [[Aina's Kitchen]] into a restaurant, and Lillie, after restoring Mohn's {{DL|Mohn|Magearna}}, sets off with Gladion and {{an|Lusamine}} to search for [[Mohn]] with Magearna's help. Bidding a [[SM146|heartfelt farewell]] to his Alolan family, Ash returns to Pallet Town, his journey leaving an indelible mark as he looks forward to new horizons. {{an|Professor Burnet}} and Kukui are revealed to be [[Lei|expecting]]. ===''Pokémon Journeys: The Series''=== {{main|Timeline of events in Pokémon Journeys: The Series|Timeline of events in ''Pokémon Journeys: The Series''}} In {{aniseries|JN}}, {{Ash}} embarks on his as-of-now last adventure as a research fellow under [[Professor Cerise]] at the [[Cerise Laboratory]] in [[Vermilion City]], teaming up with his new friend {{an|Goh}}. Together, they travel across various regions to learn more about Pokémon and their natural habitats. Goh, driven by a childhood encounter with the Mythical Pokémon {{an|Mew}}, aims to catch every Pokémon species, including Mew itself. Meanwhile, Ash enters the prestigious [[World Coronation Series]] to challenge the world's strongest Trainers and ultimately defeat the reigning Monarch, {{an|Leon}}, and get one step closer to his dream of becoming a Pokémon Master. Their journey takes them to places like the [[Galar]] region, where they witness the [[Dynamax]] phenomenon and become involved in the [[Darkest Day]] crisis concerning the Legendary Pokémon [[Leon's Eternatus|Eternatus]], [[Legendary heroes (anime)#Zacian|Zacian]], and [[Legendary heroes (anime)#Zamazenta|Zamazenta]]. Ash expands his team with powerful partners like {{AP|Pikachu}}, {{AP|Dragonite}}, {{AP|Gengar}}, {{AP|Sirfetch'd}}, {{AP|Lucario}}, and {{AP|Dracovish}}, mastering battle mechanics including [[Dynamax]], [[Gigantamax]], [[Z-Move]]s, and [[Mega Evolution]]. While Goh continues to become a better Trainer, with his {{TP|Goh|Cinderace}} and {{TP|Goh|Inteleon}} by his side, along with several new additions. They also befriend [[Chloe]] and her {{TP|Chloe|Eevee}}, and encounter Legendary Pokémon such as {{p|Mewtwo}}, {{p|Suicune}}, and {{p|Ho-Oh}}. As he climbs the ranks of the World Coronation Series, Ash reunites with old friends and rivals, including {{an|Iris}}, now the Unova Champion, and {{an|Gary}}. Notably, his former rival [[Paul]] returns, and helps Ash train for the [[Masters Eight Tournament]] by engaging him in a challenging practice battle, which helps Ash refine his strategies. In the climactic Masters Eight Tournament, Ash faces off against some of the world's most formidable Trainers, such as {{an|Cynthia}}, {{an|Steven Stone}}, and ultimately Leon. With support from his friends, including Goh and Chloe, and the experience gained from his extensive travels, Ash defeats Leon in an [[JN132|epic showdown]], becoming the new Monarch. [[JN133|Concurrently]], Goh's participation in [[Project Mew]] leads him to a significant encounter with Mew on [[Faraway Island]]. Recognizing their individual aspirations, Ash and Goh amicably [[JN136|part ways]] to pursue their respective goals—Ash continues his journey toward becoming a Pokémon Master, while Goh sets off to explore more of the Pokémon world. Continuing his journey alone, Ash reunites with his longtime friends {{an|Misty}} and {{an|Brock}}, and together they embark on new adventures that pay homage to significant moments from his past. Along the way, they encounter familiar Pokémon, such as his {{AP|Lapras}}, and his {{AP|Squirtle}}, now leading the [[Squirtle Squad]] as an esteemed firefighting team. They also cross paths with the Legendary Pokémon {{an|Latias}} and {{p|Latios}}; Ash aids Latios in escaping from a persistent Pokémon hunter, reaffirming his unwavering commitment to protecting all Pokémon. Eventually, Ash returns to Pallet Town, where he reflects on his extensive journey. Reunited with his family and old friends, he reaffirms his aspiration to become a [[Pokémon Master]]. With renewed determination and a deeper understanding of his bond with Pokémon, Ash [[JN147|sets off]] once again into the world, embracing whatever new adventures await him. ==References== {{reflist}} ==Related articles== * [[Timeline of events in Pokémon Horizons: The Series|Timeline of events in ''Pokémon Horizons: The Series'']] * [[List of animated series episodes]] * [[List of character ages]] {{Pokémon world}} {{Project Anime notice|no}} [[Category:Pokémon animated series]] [[Category:Lists]] [[es:Cronología de eventos del anime]] [[it:Cronologia degli eventi nella serie animata originale]]
